options.content:
**Two RTX 2000 Ada cards, 16,380 MiB each, time-sliced ×3 (6 allocatable `nvidia.com/gpu`).** Time-slicing gives **no memory isolation** — a CUDA OOM in one pod can take down its card-mates, so headroom is a shared budget, not a per-pod one.

### Never group DCGM series by `pod`
`DCGM_FI_DEV_*` is **per DEVICE**. dcgm-exporter decorates it with a `pod` label taken from the kubelet's *device → pod* map, and under time-slicing that label is an arbitrary pick from the pods sharing the card. Measured 2026-09-21: GPU 1 read 8,917 MiB labelled `hope-stt-worker`, while `nvidia-smi` inside `hope-lmstudio` showed its `llama-server` holding **8,908 of those MiB**. Over 6 h each device carried **five** different `pod` labels while the device count stayed at 2.

Every panel here therefore aggregates with **`max by (gpu)`**. `sum` over the raw metric would double-count the moment the exporter emits more than one series per device, and `rate()` breaks across a pod rollover because the series identity changes with the label.

> ⚠️ **These aggregations are correct for dcgm-exporter `4.4.2-4.7.0`, the version this cluster runs.** Release `4.5.3-4.8.2` (2026-05-07) added genuine per-POD attribution for `DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED` / `DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL` behind `--kubernetes-virtual-gpus`, which changes what a series *means*. **Re-verify every `max by (gpu)` here before or immediately after any dcgm-exporter upgrade** — if the metric starts carrying per-pod shares, `max` silently becomes "the largest pod" instead of "the device".

### What is measured and what is not
| Granularity | Status |
|---|---|
| **Per device** | ✅ measured — `DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED/FREE/RESERVED`, live |
| **Per process** | ⏳ needs `infrastructure/gpu-process-exporter` (TASK-996 Phase 4). Panels below are **empty until it is deployed** |
| **Per model — weights** | ⏳ needs `GET admin/inference-engines/lm-studio/runtime` (Phase 3) |
| **Per model — KV cache** | ⚠️ **ESTIMATE, never measured.** Derived from `context × parallel`. LM Studio gives every parallel slot the full context window |
| **Per thread** | ❌ **impossible.** CUDA attributes memory to a process/context; neither NVML nor DCGM exposes thread-level accounting. Struck from scope (TASK-996 D-5) |

### The pathology this dashboard exists to show
**One model resident on BOTH cards.** `--split-mode layer` spreads layers across devices when the model plus its KV cache does not fit on one, and every token then pays a PCIe hop. "Cards holding model memory" reading **2** with a single model loaded is the fault condition; **1** is healthy. Ticket: `docs/implementation/TASK-996-LM-Studio-Serving-Control-And-VRAM-Observability/README.md`.

panels.title: VRAM used per card (ceiling 16,380 MiB)
panels.description: max by (gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED), MiB → bytes. Aggregated with max, NOT sum: the pod label on this metric is unreliable under time-slicing. The ceiling is the physical card, so the gap to full is the real load budget — see 'Best single-card headroom'.

panels.title: Best single-card headroom
panels.description: max(max by (gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_FREE)) — the largest free block on ANY one card. This is the number the Phase-3 load precheck (TASK-996 D-6) must compare a model's --estimate-only against: a model larger than this cannot be loaded onto a single device and will be split across both.

panels.title: Per-card framebuffer: used / free / reserved
panels.description: The three DCGM framebuffer fields per device. used + free + reserved reconciles to 16,379 MiB, so 'reserved' (~430 MiB of driver overhead per card) is visible rather than silently eating headroom.

panels.title: Cards holding model memory  (1 = healthy · 2 = SPLIT)
panels.description: count(max by (gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED) > 512) — how many devices currently hold more than 512 MiB. With one model server loaded, 2 means llama.cpp spread the model across both cards (--split-mode layer) and every token is paying a PCIe hop. This is the fault TASK-996 R-6 / gpuSplitConfig exists to fix. NOTE: with several independent GPU workloads resident, 2 is expected — read this panel together with the per-process panels below, which is what makes it unambiguous.

panels.title: Card occupancy (% of physical framebuffer)
panels.description: 100 * used / (used + free + reserved), per device. Two lines both well above zero with a single model loaded is the cross-GPU split; the healthy shape is one card carrying the model and the other near its idle floor.

targets.expr: 100 * max by (gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED) / max by (gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED + DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_FREE + DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_RESERVED)

panels.title: PCIe traffic per card — the cost of a split model
panels.description: DCGM_FI_PROF_PCIE_TX/RX_BYTES is a GAUGE of bytes moved per DCGM sample interval, NOT a counter — it is read raw here, never through rate(), because the series is non-monotonic (observed 25,632 → 25,462 between scrapes) and rate() would also break across a pod-label rollover. Treat it as a relative indicator: a model split across both cards moves activations over PCIe on every token, so this rises and stays risen. A load event shows as a large transient spike (weights being pushed to the device).

panels.title: GPU utilisation
panels.description: max by (gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL). With time-slicing ×3 this is the DEVICE's busy fraction across every sharing pod — it cannot be attributed to one workload.

panels.title: Board power draw
panels.description: max by (gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_USAGE), watts. An idle RTX 2000 Ada with weights resident sits near 19 W; sustained decode pulls it up. Useful as a cheap 'is this card actually working or just holding memory' signal.

panels.title: GPU temperature
panels.description: max by (gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_TEMP), °C. Both cards are passed through to one node, so a rise on both at once is chassis airflow, not one workload.

panels.title: Per-process VRAM by pod  —  NO DATA until the Phase-4 exporter is deployed
panels.description: MEASURED per-process memory, joined to pod names through kube-state-metrics. Requires `infrastructure/gpu-process-exporter` (a hostPID DaemonSet running nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps). dcgm-exporter can NEVER supply per-PID data — DCGM's PID fields are binary blobs its value converter discards, and NVIDIA closed the request as out of scope (dcgm-exporter#521). Try the cheaper path FIRST: upgrading dcgm-exporter past 4.5.3-4.8.2 and enabling --kubernetes-virtual-gpus gives correctly-attributed per-POD VRAM with no new component, which may be all this cluster needs. See infrastructure/gpu-process-exporter/README.md §1. Until one of the two lands this panel is deliberately empty rather than approximated. A process appearing on TWO gpu rows with the same pid IS the cross-GPU split, named at last.

panels.title: Per-process VRAM over time  —  NO DATA until the Phase-4 exporter is deployed
panels.description: Same source as the table, unjoined so that a GPU process belonging to NO pod (a host process, pod_uid="") is still visible — the kube_pod_info join would silently drop it. Series are per (pid, gpu): one process on two cards draws two lines.

panels.title: Models each service reports running (measured)
panels.description: sum by (exported_service, model) (model_running_instances) — what the text and guardrail services say is loaded. This is the only per-MODEL signal that exists today and it is a count, not memory: LM Studio publishes no Prometheus metrics of its own. It is here so the per-device panels above can be read against a named model rather than an anonymous card.

panels.title: Per-model residency: weights (measured) vs KV cache (ESTIMATE)  —  NO DATA until Phase 3
panels.description: WEIGHTS are measured — `lms ps` SIZE, surfaced by the Phase-3 route GET admin/inference-engines/lm-studio/runtime. KV CACHE IS NOT MEASURED. It is derived as context × parallel × per-token KV bytes, because LM Studio allocates every parallel slot the FULL context window. Observed 2026-09-21: a 3.35 GB model held 13.9 GiB across both cards at context 131072 × parallel 10 — the ~10.5 GiB delta was f16 KV. Never present the estimate as a measurement; when the estimate and (device used − weights) diverge, the estimate is what is wrong.

defaults.noValue: No LM Studio runtime exporter — TASK-996 Phase 3 (GET admin/inference-engines/lm-studio/runtime) is not built
